The '''Kaleesh''', also known as the '''Kaleeshi''', were a [[Reptile|reptilian]] [[Sentience|sentient]] [[species]] from the [[Wild Space]] [[Planet|world]] of [[Kalee]]. They had [[Color|red]], scaly skin and possessed the distinctive [[snake]]-like, slitted yellow [[eye]]s, a flat or snub [[nose]], and elongated, pointed [[ear]]s, surrounded by two enormous [[Tooth|tusks]] on their lower jaws. A primal yet spiritual people, the Kaleesh were formidable [[Soldier|warriors]], and they were not likely to display empathy, kindness, or vulnerability. All Kaleesh nearly always concealed their facial features behind terrifying customary [[Kaleesh mask|war masks]], which were typically crafted from the [[Bone|skulls]], bones, and teeth of the deadliest [[Diet|predatory]] beasts on their home planet—[[mumuu]], [[erkush]], and [[karabbac]].

Despite their technological inferiority, the fierce and [[Kaleesh warrior|proud warriors]] engaged in numerous conflicts, particularly against the [[Yam'rii]], their technologically superior adversary and planetary neighbor, an [[insect]]oid species of the desolate planet [[Huk]] in the [[Star system|system]] of the [[Huk system|same name]] near [[Kalee system|their own]]. The most notorious member of the species, [[General]] [[Grievous]], fought as the [[Supreme Martial Commander of the Separatist Droid Armies]] during the [[Clone Wars]].

==Biology and appearance==
[[File:KaleeshUnmasked-AORGrievous1.png|thumb|left|200px|Grievous' face before being cybernetically enhanced]]
The Kaleesh,<ref name="KaleeshDB" /> also known as the Kaleeshi,<ref name="After the Fall">{{StoryCite|story=After the Fall|book=The High Republic: Tales of Light and Life}}</ref> were a [[species]] of [[Color|red]]-skinned<ref name="EpisodeIII" /> [[humanoid]]<ref name="KaleeshDB" /> [[Reptile|reptilians]]<ref name="CharacterEncyclopediaUAE" /> from<ref name="Alien Archive" /> the wilderness<ref name="Hyperspace Stories: Grievous">''[[Hyperspace Stories: Grievous]]''</ref> of the [[planet]] [[Kalee]]<ref name="Beginnings" /> in [[Wild Space]],<ref name="TFABG">[[Star Wars: The Force Awakens Beginner Game|''Star Wars: The Force Awakens'' Beginner Game]]</ref> having distinctive [[snake]]-like<ref name="Alien Archive" /> beady<ref name="Saber Truth">{{InsiderCite|210|Galactic Tales: Saber Truth}}</ref> yellow eyes<ref name="EpisodeIII" /> with slit pupils<ref name="Alien Archive" /> and eyelids<ref name="Grievous Intrigue">{{TCW|Grievous Intrigue}}</ref> framed by prominent brows, triangular-shaped [[nose|nostrils]] with two slits toward their eyes, and a [[mouth]]<ref name="lair" /> with [[Tooth|teeth]],<ref name="AOR">[[Age of Republic - General Grievous 1|''Age of Republic - General Grievous'' 1]]</ref> two of which are fangs in the upper jaw, which, when closed, are visible. Two<ref name="lair" /> large<ref name="HC 30">{{HelmetCollectionCite|30|Databank A-Z}}</ref> tusks protruded<ref name="lair" /> from the lower jaws<ref name="HC 30" /> on both sides,<ref name="lair" /> and bony protrusions jutted from the chin.<ref name="Star Wars 100 Objects" /><ref name="AOR" /> Although all of their facial features were reminiscent of [[bat]]s, such as their elongated,<ref name="KaleeshDB" /> pointed<ref name="The Missing Agent">{{Resistance|The Missing Agent}}</ref> [[ear]]s and flat<ref name="KaleeshDB" /> or snub<ref name="Star Wars 100 Objects" /> [[nose]]s, they usually wore [[Helmet|masks]].<ref name="KaleeshDB" /> Their two [[Limb|arms]] were long and thin, with four-fingered hands,<ref name="lair" /> two of which possessed opposable thumbs,<ref name="Star Wars 100 Objects" /> had sharp, [[claw]]-like nails on each,<ref name="The Missing Agent" /><ref name="AOR" /> and two four-jointed legs,<ref name="lair" /> bent back,<ref name="Almost a Jedi">{{StoryCite|story=Almost a Jedi|book=The Clone Wars: Stories of Light and Dark}}</ref> with five-toed scute feet: two in front, two on each side, and one in the back.<ref name="lair" />

They were digitigrades,<ref name="lair" /> walking on their toes rather than their entire feet,<ref name="Alien Archive" /> and they possessed a [[brain]],<ref name="SWEasy">''[[Star Wars Made Easy]]''</ref> a [[heart]], [[lung]]s,<ref name="AEYNK">''[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know]]''</ref> a [[liver]],<ref name="Star Wars 100 Objects" /> several vital internal organs,<ref name="CVD">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary, New Edition]]''</ref> and nerve endings.<ref name="Droid with a Heart">{{StoryCite|story=The Droid with a Heart|book=Myths & Fables}}</ref> Their internal organs were extremely flammable.<ref name="EpisodeIII" /><ref name="The Complete Saga">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]''</ref> The species had two [[Gender|sexes]], male<ref name="EpisodeIII" /> and female.<ref name="After the Fall" /> Their claws ranged from white<ref name="AOR" /> to black.<ref name="The Missing Agent" /> Like other reptiles, Kaleesh are cold-[[blood]]ed and could recognize one when they see it and have scaly skin. As if prepared to strike, their scales quivered menacingly.<ref name="After the Fall" /> Kaleesh perceive color in their eyesight<ref name="Complete Vehicles 2018">[[Star Wars: Complete Vehicles (2018)|''Star Wars: Complete Vehicles'' (2018)]]</ref> and could also smell an individual's origin and the stench of death from afar.<ref name="Battlefront II" />

==Society and culture==
[[File:GrievousStatue-SW100Objects.png|thumb|right|250px|A statue of Grievous holding the severed head of a [[Skrilling]].]]
Though primitive,<ref name="The Separatists">{{EncyclopediaCite|The Separatists}}</ref> the Kaleesh were a fierce<ref name="UltimateCookbook">''[[Star Wars: The Ultimate Cookbook]]''</ref> and proud<ref name="lair" /> culture of [[Soldier|warriors]]<ref name="HC 8">{{HelmetCollectionCite|8|Helmets}}</ref> who were known for their lack of mercy.<ref name="Battlefront II" /> [[Dumas Mar'Ti]] was a Kaleesh who believed in a pantheon of beings she called her [[god]]s. According to Mar'Ti, her [[sin]]s were a matter between her and the gods.<ref name="After the Fall" /> One of their [[Deity|deities]] was called [[Ithano (god)|Ithano]] and was a trickster god.<ref name="BinaryStar">{{InsiderCite|234|Galactic Tales: The Crimson Corsair and the Sinister Secret of the Binary Star}}</ref> The [[warlord]]s of Kalee were worshipped by a young [[Grievous]], who would watch the warlords return home with plunders taken in war.<ref name="The Dark Side">''[[Star Wars: The Dark Side]]''</ref>

On their [[homeworld]] of Kalee, [[Kaleesh warrior]]s [[Hunting|hunted]] [[mumuu]], [[erkush]], and [[karabbac]]. Instead of only hunting for [[Foodstuff|meat]] alone,<ref name="UltimateCookbook" /> they generally killed to demonstrate their bravery<ref name="BC 65">{{BustCollectionCite|65|Character}}</ref> and make masks and [[Clothing|clothing]]. Whereas the clothing was made from the animal hides,<ref name="UltimateCookbook" /> those fearsome [[Kaleesh mask|traditional masks]]<ref name="HC 8" /> were frequently<ref name="HC 59" /> carved from the [[Bone|skulls]], bones,<ref name="HC 8" /> and teeth<ref name="German HC 8">{{HelmetCollectionCite|8|Helmets}} (German version)</ref> of the deadliest [[diet|predatory]] beasts.<ref name="HC 8" /> With that mask in hand, a Kaleesh's features were normally<ref name="Alien Archive" /> and traditionally<ref name="HC 8" /> hidden behind the mask, with only their slitted golden<ref name="Alien Archive" /> eyes and tusks visible.<ref name="lair" />

Before battle, Kaleesh smeared<ref name="Star Wars 100 Objects">''[[Star Wars 100 Objects]]''</ref> karabbac-blood war paint above their eyes on their skull masks.<ref name="HC 8" /> Rarely seen without these masks, their masks also made it difficult to read their expressions.<ref name="TCC">{{StoryCite|story=The Crimson Corsair and the Lost Treasure of Count Dooku|book=Tales from a Galaxy Far, Far Away: Aliens: Volume I}}</ref><ref name="UltimateCookbook" /> Apparently, if it were discovered that someone wore a similar mask just for effect, the Kaleesh would not tolerate it.<ref name="TFA head to head">''[[Star Wars: The Force Awakens: Head-to-Head]]''</ref> Kaleesh dressed in<ref name="lair" /> campaign<ref name="Ships and Vehicles 55">{{ShipsandVehiclesCite|55|History of the Ship}}</ref> [[Kaleesh cloak|cloaks]] and [[Clothing|half hoods]] with headwear<ref name="lair" /> as part of their homeworld's warrior traditions, giving them a menacing appearance,<ref name="HC 24">{{HelmetCollectionCite|24|Weapons & Uniforms}}</ref> and used [[weapon]]s including [[sword]]s, [[Shield (physical armor)|shields]], [[spear]]s,<ref name="lair" /> and [[slugthrower]]s,<ref name="English Separatists" /> such as the [[Czerka Arms]] [[Outland rifle]].<ref name="The Separatists" /> Kaleesh warriors developed [[Kaleesh martial arts|their own]] [[Unarmed combat|martial disciplines]]. The Jedi appropriated their<ref name="The Glass Abyss">''[[Mace Windu: The Glass Abyss]]''</ref> ancient<ref name="TGAGerman">''[[Mace Windu: The Glass Abyss]]'' {{C|German version only}}</ref> techniques into an unarmed combat style known as "[[Na Jang]]" and utilized it to train<ref name="The Glass Abyss" /> various<ref name="TGAGerman" /> military units<ref name="The Glass Abyss" /> across the [[galaxy]].<ref name="TGAGerman" />

==History==
===Wars with the Bitthævrian and Yam'rii===
At one point, Kaleesh warlords<ref name="Falcon 65">{{BuildFalconCite|65|Guide to the Galaxy}}</ref> and warriors<ref name="German Falcon 65">[[Star Wars: Build the Millennium Falcon 65|''Star Wars: Build the Millennium Falcon'' 65]] {{C|German version}}</ref> took [[roggwart]]s as trophies<ref name="Falcon 65" /> from the battles with the [[Bitthævrian]]<ref name="German Falcon 65" /> on [[Guiteica]],<ref name="Falcon 65" /> Bitthævrian homeworld<ref name="Falcon 65" /> that neighbored Kalee.<ref name="Topps Star Wars Hyperspace">{{Topps|set=2024 Topps Star Wars Hyperspace|cardname=Roggwarts – Mustafar}}</ref>

The overextended [[Galactic Republic|Old Republic]] overlooked crimes on numerous peripheral worlds. One such world was Kalee, which unintentionally faced injustice at their hands. The low-tech Kaleesh were conquered by the [[insect]]oid the [[Yam'rii]]<ref name="The Separatists" /> of the desolate planet [[Huk]]<ref name="Ships and Vehicles 55" /> in the [[Huk system]]<ref name="Appendix">{{GalaxyMapAppendix}}</ref> next to<ref name="HC 8" /> [[Kalee system|Kalee's own]].<ref name="Appendix" /> The Yam'rii had ruthlessly invaded many worlds in their [[Huk sector|sector]], stripping them of their resources and selling their populations into [[slavery]]. When they focused their attention on Kaleesh's homeworld, the results were horrifying and resulted in a never-ending,<ref name="The Separatists" /> [[Kaleesh-Yam'rii war|merciless conflict]]<ref name="HC 8" /> between the Kaleesh and Yam'rii.<ref name="The Separatists" />

===Rise of Grievous===
Born on Kalee amidst the near-continual conflict against the Huk,<ref name="The Separatists" /> a Kaleesh named Qymaen jai Sheelal,<ref name="Build R2-D2 57">{{BuildR2Cite|57|Droid Directory}}</ref> who later became known as Grievous,<ref name="BDOWD">{{EncyclopediaCite|Battle Droids and Other Droids of War}}</ref> would become a warlord<ref name="The Dark Side" /> and learn the art of warfare and battle tactics,<ref name="Rise">''[[Rise of the Separatists]]''</ref> specifically tactics that were ruthless and successful,<ref name="The Dark Side" /> in his homeworld's battle<ref name="Rise" /> against the Huk.<ref name="The Separatists" /> Gathering them<ref name="English Separatists">{{EncyclopediaCite|The Separatists}} {{C|English version}}</ref> as his [[bodyguard]]s, Grievous fought alongside his people's strongest warriors,<ref name="The Separatists" /> the [[Izvoshra]],<ref name="BDOWD" /> over the [[Standard year|years]] of war. With increased ferocity and determination,<ref name="The Separatists" /> Grievous led his people in a ruthless<ref name="HC 8" /> all-war against the Yam'rii,<ref name="English Separatists" /> carrying out an offensive. In [[time]], the Kaleesh forces successfully repelled the Yam'rii from their world.<ref name="The Separatists" /> Grievous launched a series of devastating campaigns on Huk itself,<ref name="Ships and Vehicles 55" /> sweeping across the barren Huk worlds.<ref name="English Ships and Vehicles 55">{{ShipsandVehiclesCite|55|History of the Ship}} (English version)</ref> However, the Yam'rii pulled off an unexpected move and appealed to the Republic for assistance.<ref name="The Separatists" /> The Republic<ref name="Rise" /> and the [[Jedi]] intervened,<ref name="HC 8" /> siding with the Yam'rii<ref name="Rise" /> against the Kaleesh invaders. The Kaleesh were censured and faced a mixture of embargoes and fines, leaving hundreds of thousands to die of starvation.<ref name="The Separatists" />

[[File:GeneralGrievousBattleDroids-BFII.png|thumb|left|300px|The cyborg warlord Grievous started out his life as an organic Kaleesh and embraced his rage, becoming Supreme Commander of the Separatist Droid Army.]]
Developing a personal vendetta against them,<ref name="Rise" /> Grievous's hatred for the Republic and the Jedi only increased.<ref name="The Separatists" /> It may have been the hatred he felt that drove Grievous to join<ref name="The Separatists" /> the [[InterGalactic Banking Clan]].<ref name="BDOWD" /> Proving to be phenomenally successful, he became one of the IGBC's more valuable resources. By that time, [[Count]] [[Dooku]] and [[Darth Sidious]] had already taken notice of his exploits and had major plans for him.<ref name="The Separatists" /> The [[Sith]] approached Grievous with the ability to be transformed into a [[cyborg]], to which Grievous agreed<ref name="The Dark Side" /> and, over time, replaced his body with cybernetic implants.<ref name="SWEasy">''[[Star Wars Made Easy]]''</ref> With his upgrades, Grievous increased his power<ref name="CVD">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary, New Edition]]''</ref> and skill.<ref name="Ultimate Star Wars">''[[Ultimate Star Wars]]''</ref>

However, one day, [[Grievous' shuttle]] was [[Sabotage of Grievous' shuttle|sabotaged]]<ref name="Galaxy at War">''[[Star Wars: A Galaxy at War]]''</ref> during an assassination attempt planned by [[San Hill]],<ref name="Star Wars: Masterwork">{{Topps|set=2019 Topps Star Wars Masterwork|cardname=General Grievous}}</ref> causing his [[troop carrier]] to crash and fling him from the debris.<ref name="German HC 8">{{HelmetCollectionCite|8|Helmets}} (German version)</ref> The sabotage nearly killed him<ref name="Galaxy at War" /> and destroyed the majority<ref name="Alien Archive" /> of his original body.<ref name="Alien Archive" /> After being taken from his homeworld,<ref name="Grievous">''[[Hyperspace Stories: Grievous]]''</ref> he regained consciousness in a [[bacta tank]] and discovered that he had been nearly entirely gutted and deformed by [[Surgeon|surgical]] [[FX-series medical assistant droid|FX droids]].<ref name="German Build X-Wing 47">{{BuildXWingCite|47|Starfighter Aces}} (German edition)</ref> In order to survive his injuries,<ref name="Build X-Wing 47">{{BuildXWingCite|47|Starfighter Aces}}</ref> he was further transformed into a cyborg<ref name="lair" /> and served as the [[Commander]] of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems|Separatist]] [[Droid]] Army, bringing him face-to-face with the despised Jedi and seizing their [[lightsaber]]s as trophies throughout the years until his [[death]] on [[Utapau]].<ref name="EpisodeIII" />

==Kaleesh in the galaxy==
{{Quote|I met a Kaleesh on my travels who bragged of a revered warrior. He supposedly had cybernetic implants for enhanced combat!|An [[Unidentified artist|artist]] learns of Grievous|<ref name="Alien Archive" />}}
During the [[High Republic Era]], the Kaleesh Dumas Mar'Ti was a [[captain]] of her own [[starship]], the ''[[Athos]]'', and a member of the [[Byne Guild]].<ref name="After the Fall">{{StoryCite|story=After the Fall|book=The High Republic: Tales of Light and Life}}</ref> One of the species' most well-known members was [[General]] Grievous, who was also regarded as its most infamous.<ref name="Alien Archive" /> His mostly [[Cybernetics|cybernetic]] body eliminated most resemblance to other Kaleesh.<ref name="GrievousSWE">{{SWE|characters|generalgrievous|General Grievous}}</ref> As the [[Supreme Martial Commander of the Separatist Droid Armies|Supreme Commander]] of the [[Separatist Droid Army]], he fought in the Clone Wars<ref name="ForceCollection LS Grievous">{{ForceCollection|General Grievous [Last Stand]|star=5}}</ref> until he was killed by [[Jedi General]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] during the [[Battle of Utapau]].<ref name="EpisodeIII" />

Though not Kaleesh himself,<ref name="HC 59">{{HelmetCollectionCite|59|Helmets}}</ref> the [[Delphidian]] [[pirate]] [[captain]] [[Sidon Ithano]] wore a red [[plasteel]] [[Sidon Ithano's helmet|mask]] that resembled<ref name="Lost Treasure">"[[The Crimson Corsair and the Lost Treasure of Count Dooku]]"</ref> that of the ruthless<ref name="Chewbacca">{{EncyclopediaCite|Chewbacca and Other Aliens of the Rebellion and the Resistance}}</ref> reptilian Kaleesh species,<ref name="Kaleesh Databank">{{Databank|kaleesh|Kaleesh}}</ref> one of the masks<ref name="HC 59" /> he stole from the Kaleesh,<ref name="AEYNK" /> to hide his Delphidian heritage.<ref name="HC 59" /> During the [[First Order-Resistance War]],<ref name="Battles">''[[Star Wars: Battles that Changed the Galaxy]]''</ref> one Kaleesh was present at the [[Vargo Spaceport]] on the planet [[Varkana]], wandering around when the [[First Order]] [[First Order stormtrooper|stormtroopers]] [[Rescue of Norath Kev|searched the city]] for [[resistance]] [[spy]] [[Norath Kev]].<ref name="The Missing Agent" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Kaleesh first appeared in the [[2005]] film ''[[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith]]'', directed by [[George Lucas]].<ref name="EpisodeIII" />

In the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, the [[Kaleesh/Legends|Kaleesh]] first appeared in the animated television series ''[[Star Wars: Clone Wars]]'' [[Clone Wars: Season Two|season two]], the tenth and final episode, "[[Chapter 20 (Star Wars: Clone Wars)|Chapter 20]]," directed by [[Genndy Tartakovsky]],<ref name="Clone Wars 20">{{CW|20}}</ref> which aired on [[April 8]], [[2004]] on [[Cartoon Network]].<ref name="Episode date">{{TVcom|url=shows/star-wars-clone-wars/chapter-xx-276626|text=''Star Wars: Clone Wars'' – Season 1, Episode 20: Chapter XX}}</ref> The species was later [[Retroactive continuity|retconned]] to be mentioned in multiple other sources, including "[[Heir to the Empire]]", the first installment of [[Star Wars: The Thrawn Trilogy]], written by [[Timothy Zahn]] and published in [[May 6]] [[1991]].<ref name="HTTE">''[[Heir to the Empire]]''</ref>
